formulation.rationale: The mapped products are insulin degludec with unspecified concentration, U-100, or U-200. The compared perioperative society guidance either names degludec directly or addresses long-acting basal analogues and does not distinguish U-100 from U-200 for fasting management.

comparisons.checked_locators: Table 2, Basal insulin (ultra-long-acting insulin analog: Degludec); Important note 11
comparisons.note: The joint statement explicitly names degludec and provides pre-procedure dose-reduction timing, conditional dose modification based on basal proportion, and a no-omission rule for absolute insulin deficiency.

comparisons.checked_locators: Perioperative Care; Insulin Therapy Recommendations 16.8 and 16.9
comparisons.note: ADA provides perioperative long-acting basal-insulin adjustment and supports basal insulin during both NPO/poor-intake and adequate-intake states.

comparisons.checked_locators: Recommendations Before Colonoscopy > Patient Education and Navigation
comparisons.note: The current US colonoscopy consensus leaves antihyperglycemic medication management to individualized planning with the prescribing clinician and does not give a degludec-specific dose.

recommendations.timing_text: Reducing the dose 20%-30%, starting 72 h before the procedure
recommendations.strength: not separately stated in table row
recommendations.certainty: not separately stated in table row
recommendations.applicability: Elective procedure in a patient receiving ultra-long-acting insulin degludec.
recommendations.exceptions: The same table provides different handling for high basal-insulin proportions and for basal-bolus regimens with less than 50% of total daily insulin as basal.
recommendations.summary: The 2026 Brazilian joint statement recommends reducing degludec by 20%-30% starting 72 hours before the procedure.

recommendations.timing_text: In patients receiving a high proportion of basal insulin (> 50% of total daily insulin), consider reducing the dose by up to 50%.
recommendations.strength: not separately stated in table row
recommendations.certainty: not separately stated in table row
recommendations.applicability: Degludec regimen in which basal insulin constitutes more than 50% of total daily insulin.
recommendations.summary: The Brazilian joint statement allows a larger reduction, up to 50%, when basal insulin exceeds 50% of total daily insulin.

recommendations.qualifier: basal-bolus regimen with lower basal proportion
recommendations.timing_text: dose reduction may not be necessary
recommendations.strength: not separately stated in table row
recommendations.certainty: not separately stated in table row
recommendations.applicability: Basal-bolus regimen in which less than 50% of total daily insulin is basal.
recommendations.exceptions: The source states that maintaining the usual basal dose may help prevent hyperglycemia and glycemic variability.
recommendations.summary: For basal-bolus regimens with less than 50% of total daily insulin as basal, the Brazilian joint statement says dose reduction may not be necessary.

recommendations.timing_text: On the evening before surgery, reduce long-acting basal insulin analogs to 75–80% of the usual dose
recommendations.strength: not separately graded in this narrative instruction
recommendations.certainty: not separately graded in this narrative instruction
recommendations.applicability: Long-acting basal insulin analogue use before surgery; degludec is an ultra-long-acting basal analogue.
recommendations.exceptions: ADA states that adjustment depends on diabetes type and clinical judgment.
recommendations.summary: ADA recommends reducing long-acting basal insulin analogues to 75–80% of the usual dose on the evening before surgery.

recommendations.timing_text: Basal insulin or a basal plus bolus correction insulin plan is the preferred treatment
recommendations.applicability: Noncritically ill patient with poor oral intake or taking nothing by mouth.
recommendations.exceptions: This recommendation establishes continuation of a basal component but does not specify a degludec dose.
recommendations.summary: ADA recommends retaining basal insulin as part of the preferred insulin plan when oral intake is poor or the patient is NPO.

recommendations.timing_text: must never have basal insulin omitted
recommendations.applicability: Type 1 diabetes, LADA, or status after total pancreatectomy with absolute insulin deficiency.
recommendations.exceptions: The source permits omission only when the patient is receiving continuous intravenous insulin infusion or a fully functional subcutaneous insulin pump.
recommendations.summary: The Brazilian joint statement says basal insulin must not be omitted in patients with absolute insulin deficiency except when alternative continuous insulin delivery is in place.

recommendations.qualifier: post-procedure poor oral intake or NPO
recommendations.timing_text: Basal insulin or a basal plus bolus correction insulin plan is the preferred treatment
recommendations.applicability: Post-procedure noncritically ill patient with poor oral intake or still NPO.
recommendations.exceptions: The source does not specify a fixed post-procedure degludec dose or restart time.
recommendations.summary: When oral intake remains poor or the patient remains NPO, ADA retains basal insulin in the preferred post-procedure insulin plan.

recommendations.timing_text: an insulin plan with basal, prandial, and correction components is the preferred treatment
recommendations.applicability: Noncritically ill patient with adequate nutritional intake after the procedure.
recommendations.exceptions: The source does not specify a fixed degludec restart interval or patient-specific dose.
recommendations.summary: With adequate nutritional intake, ADA includes basal insulin as part of the preferred insulin plan.

scenario_coverage.reason: SBD/SBA/ABESO gives degludec-specific dose-reduction timing and conditional modifications; ADA gives a broader long-acting basal analogue adjustment.
ADA retains basal insulin during NPO/poor intake, and SBD/SBA/ABESO states basal insulin must not be omitted in absolute insulin deficiency.
ADA includes basal insulin in preferred regimens for both poor/NPO and adequate nutritional intake states.

conflicts.description: The Brazilian joint statement gives degludec-specific adjustment beginning 72 hours before the procedure, whereas ADA gives a broader long-acting basal-analogue adjustment on the evening before surgery. The timing frameworks are preserved separately rather than harmonized.

open_questions.text: USMSTF does not provide a colonoscopy-specific degludec dose and directs individualized antihyperglycemic medication planning with the prescribing clinician.
The compared sources do not distinguish Tresiba U-100 from U-200 for perioperative fasting management; no concentration-specific difference is inferred.

editorial.notes: Unreviewed evidence package. The degludec-specific Brazilian timing and the broader ADA evening-before basal-analogue adjustment are both retained because they are not identical. No patient-specific insulin dose is calculated.
